headline_marked: Myanmar Coast: [[Over 500 feared dead]] in twin boat capsizes
headline: Myanmar Coast: Over 500 feared dead in twin boat capsizes
summary: UN agencies express deep concern as two boats carrying Rohingya refugees attempting to flee Myanmar sink, potentially claiming over 500 lives. The perilous sea route has become one of the world's deadliest.
details: The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) have jointly reported that two boats carrying over 500 people have capsized off the coast of Myanmar. The passengers were attempting to escape the conflict-ridden country by sea, seeking safer shores.

The boats, believed to be carrying mostly Rohingya refugees, departed from Myanmar's Rakhine State in late June. Some passengers were reportedly from the refugee camps in Bangladesh, adding to the tragedy of the situation.

While the exact number of casualties is yet to be officially confirmed, UNHCR and IOM have voiced grave concerns over the potential loss of over 500 lives. The first boat, with approximately 250 people, lost contact shortly after departure. The second, carrying around 280 individuals, is thought to have sunk near Myanmar's Irrawaddy coast on July 8.

For years, Rohingya have risked their lives on small wooden boats to reach Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand, fleeing violence in their homeland and the harsh conditions of crowded refugee camps in Bangladesh.

The Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal have become increasingly perilous for refugees and migrants. According to UN data, nearly 900 Rohingya refugees died or went missing in these waters last year, marking it as one of the world's deadliest sea routes.

headline_marked: Bangladesh's Rabab Fatima to lead UN mission in [[Afghanistan]]
headline: Bangladesh's Rabab Fatima to lead UN mission in Afghanistan
summary: UN Secretary-General appoints Bangladeshi diplomat as new special representative
details: Rabab Fatima, a seasoned Bangladeshi diplomat, has been appointed as the new special representative for Afghanistan and head of the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA). She succeeds Roza Otunbayeva of Kyrgyzstan.

Fatima brings over 30 years of experience in national and international civil service, including bilateral and multilateral diplomacy, policymaking, and advocacy. She previously served as Bangladesh's ambassador to the UN in New York and as under-secretary-general for the Least Developed Countries.

Fatima has held various positions at Bangladesh missions in New York, Geneva, Beijing, and Kolkata, as well as at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. She has also worked at the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the Commonwealth Secretariat in London.
